reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 67 --verse 7.18.17: Sāyaṇa glosses ādhreṇa cit as daridreṇāpi sudāsā (through Sudās, even though poor, Indra caused one chief act of giving), and closes tāny etāni trīṇi karmāṇi asaṃbhāvitānīti nāśaṅkanīyāni indrasya mahimno ’dhikatvāt, which carries the weak one as Sudas when poor and the three deeds not to be doubted as impossible because Indra’s greatness exceeds them. Sudās is named in his own words (Wilson’s translation omits him), so this is Sāyaṇa and not Wilson; Wilson’s and Griffith’s notes agree on the impossible-deeds sense. "when poor" for daridreṇāpi is a fair gloss. day.js: 7.18 tells Indra’s help to Sudas against his foes in battle, 17 of 25 is late, and the key (three whole sentences, stopping before the verse’s last) names three marvels; the battle is stated in one plain clause. verse.js ok (7.18.17 at [533,17]); entry-check ok (44 words). No school, comparison or tone issue; no Nirukta treatment.
